report.summary: Found two concrete bugs: (1) snapshot_from_ledger (line ~315) treats a numeric string as intent id, so an effect key like '42' returns intent #42 instead of resolving by effect key. (2) record_offload_result (line ~220) assumes dirty_unreverted key always exists when rolled_back is true; missing key leads to applied=False, concealing uncommitted changes. Additional concerns: watch_stream swallows all exceptions without logging (line ~110), heartbeat threads in track_call may write concurrently to progress log (lack of thread safety doc). Incomplete slice – snapshot_from_bridge and snapshot_any
risks: snapshot_from_ledger: numeric string confusion – call with effect_key='123' queries by id=123 first, may return wrong intent or None.
record_offload_result: if result['rolled_back'] is true but 'dirty_unreverted' key missing, applied becomes False (instead of True) even if files left dirty.
watch_stream: exception swallowing hides all progress recording failures; no recovery or fallback logging.
track_call: heartbeat thread writes to progress log concurrently without explicit thread-safety guarantee for P.heartbeat.
Audit limited – snapshot_from_bridge and snapshot_any not visible in provided slice; potential issues there unknown.
todos: Fix snapshot_from_ledger: disambiguate effect key vs id (e.g., try effect string first, then fallback to int id if input is numeric and not matched).
Audit offload.py to ensure dirty_unreverted always present when rolled_back; or handle missing key as error.
Consider logging exceptions in watch_stream to stderr or dedicated error log for diagnostics.
Verify P.heartbeat thread safety; if not, document and perhaps protect with lock in heartbeat thread.
